portInfo.description: The City of Key West Port & Marine Services describes consolidation of deep-water cruise-ship and Navy-vessel coordination and states that the Port of Key West consists of three docking facilities: Mallory Square Dock, Pier B (privately owned), and the Navy Mole. City history notes Mallory Dock was improved in 1984 into a full cruise docking facility and cites older passenger volumes (e.g., FY1999) that must not be treated as current statistics. Separately, Keys News reported on 7 May 2026 that the Navy terminated the city’s Outer Mole lease with effective date 3 August 2026, noting the Outer Mole had served large cruise ships until 2020. For SeaDays research, Mallory and Pier B remain the evidenced civilian cruise options; Outer Mole cruise availability after lease end is an explicit gap.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Ask the line which of Mallory vs Pier B you are using; do not assume Outer Mole after the Aug 2026 Navy lease termination.
